title: API 510 Training in St. Louis: Pressure Vessel Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 510 exam prep for St. Louis and Metro East vessel inspectors: Wood River units, Missouri and Illinois vessel law, instructor Q&A.
h1: API 510 training in St. Louis: exam preparation for pressure vessel inspectors at the Wood River refinery, Metro East chemical plants and Missouri process sites
html:
API 510 exam prep for pressure vessel inspectors around St. Louis

Most of the St. Louis region's refinery pressure vessels stand on the Illinois bank of the Mississippi. The Wood River refinery at Roxana, in Madison County, runs crude, vacuum, coking, cracking, reforming and hydroprocessing units, each with its columns, drums, reactors and exchanger shells under an owner-user inspection programme. South of East St. Louis, the Sauget industrial area adds chemical operations such as Afton Chemical's fuel and lubricant additive plant, and the Missouri side contributes the deaerators, receivers and process vessels of utilities and manufacturers. Reading each vessel's thickness history, deciding what it can still hold and saying when it must be opened again is the job the API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspector certification describes.

Atlantis NDT offers exam preparation for it. The course is self-paced and online, and an instructor answers your questions while you study. There is no Atlantis classroom in St. Louis, and you do not need one: the material sits on the learning portal, and Atlantis's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. The American Petroleum Institute decides who is eligible, administers the examination at Prometric test centres and issues the certification to candidates who pass.

The Wood River refinery, unit by unit, in EIA's 2026 figures

The U.S. Energy Information Administration's Refinery Capacity Report counts operable refineries as of January 2026. It lists four in Illinois with 1,053,023 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation between them, and none in Missouri, so a St. Louis vessel inspector's refinery work happens across the river. Wood River is the largest of the four. The report still files it under WRB Refining LP, shown as 50% Phillips 66 and 50% Cenovus; Phillips 66's own results say it completed the purchase of Cenovus's half in October 2025 and has consolidated the whole refinery since then.

Hydrocarbon Processing reported in 2011 that an expansion at Wood River had started a new coker and enhanced the plant's ability to process heavy Canadian crude. Heavy, sour feed puts a recognisable set of damage mechanisms at the top of a vessel inspector's list, and it pays to know which of them the examination tests.

Matching Wood River's units to the API 510 damage mechanism list

For the September 2026, January 2027 and May 2027 windows, the API 510 Body of Knowledge limits API RP 571 questions to its definitions section and fifteen named mechanisms. Nearly every one has a home somewhere on the plot at Roxana:

  • Sulfidation and naphthenic acid corrosion in the hot sections of the crude, vacuum and coker units, where crude acidity and sulfur meet temperature.
  • Hydrochloric acid corrosion in the crude column overhead system, where chlorides that slip past the desalter condense into acid.
  • High-temperature H2/H2S corrosion and high-temperature hydrogen attack in hydrocracker and hydrotreater reactor circuits, which EIA lists at Wood River for naphtha, gasoline, jet, diesel and residual streams.
  • Wet H2S damage and amine stress corrosion cracking in the amine regenerators, sour water strippers and sulfur recovery vessels that a plant with more than a thousand short tons a day of sulfur capacity needs.
  • Caustic corrosion and caustic stress corrosion cracking wherever caustic is used for treating or neutralising.
  • Corrosion under insulation, atmospheric corrosion and brittle fracture on the outside of insulated drums and on thick vessels tested or started up cold.
  • Boiler water and steam condensate corrosion in the steam system that every refinery and chemical plant depends on.

Some of what a Wood River inspector deals with is not on that list. Polythionic acid stress corrosion cracking of austenitic stainless steel during hydroprocessing shutdowns, and the ammonium salt problems of reactor effluent systems, are real work for an inspection department but sit outside the examined paragraphs. Study them for the job and the fifteen for the exam, and check the list again for your own window, because API revises it.

Boilers' cousins: the unfired vessels around steam plants

Power boilers built to ASME Section I are outside API 510, but the unfired vessels around them are not. Deaerators, blowdown tanks, condensate receivers, flash drums and plant air receivers are usually Section VIII vessels, and owner-user programmes at refineries, chemical plants and large manufacturers frequently include them alongside process equipment. Their damage is mostly the boiler water and steam condensate corrosion that RP 571 describes, from dissolved oxygen and carbon dioxide where the water or condensate is poorly treated.

On the Missouri side, the Division of Fire Safety says it issues about 25,000 certificates of inspection a year, and it lists air compressor tanks over 10 cubic feet or above 200 psi among the objects it certifies, along with boilers and water heaters. Inspectors who know those vessels already understand thickness surveys and relief valves; API 510 adds remaining life, intervals, repairs, alterations and rerating.

Two states, two vessel laws, one metro area

An API certificate shows you know the inspection code. It does not license you to sign a state certificate inspection, and around St. Louis the law changes at the river.

Missouri

Missouri's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act, sections 650.200 to 650.295 of the Revised Statutes, is administered by the Division of Fire Safety's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Unit in Jefferson City under rules at 11 CSR 40-2. Section 650.260 sets a certificate inspection every two years for pressure vessels subject to internal corrosion and lets the board set the interval for vessels that are not, and the board may allow longer intervals. Section 650.245 lets the state commission special inspectors employed by an insurer, or employed full time by a company that keeps a regularly established inspection service for pressure vessels it operates; the inspector must pass the state examination or hold a National Board commission or an equivalent state certificate. Section 650.230 takes certain vessels out of the act altogether, among them vessels under federal control and pressure vessels used to transport and store compressed gases, a category that includes LPG containers meeting NFPA or US DOT standards.

Illinois

Wood River, Hartford and Sauget fall under the Illinois State Fire Marshal's boiler and pressure vessel law, including its rules for owner-user inspection programmes. The Chicago page for this course explains those owner-user rules, so they are not repeated here. The practical point for a candidate is the same on both banks: the Body of Knowledge warns that some jurisdictions codify older code editions in their own rules, while the examination always uses the editions on the effectivity sheet. The difference between an API certificate and a commission is set out in API 510 versus a National Board commission.

Worked example: sizing the cover fillet on a new nozzle

The Body of Knowledge asks candidates to convert a fillet weld's throat to its leg with the factor 0.7 and to check attachment welds at openings against UW-16. Take a nozzle detail from Figure UW-16.1 that calls for a cover fillet with throat tc, on a drum with a 0.625 in. shell and an NPS 4 Schedule 80 nozzle neck, 0.337 in. thick.

  1. tmin is the smaller of 0.75 in. and the thinner of the parts joined: 0.337 in.
  2. 0.7 × tmin = 0.7 × 0.337 = 0.236 in.
  3. tc must be at least the smaller of 0.25 in. and 0.236 in., so the required throat is 0.236 in.
  4. Convert to a leg: 0.236 ÷ 0.7 = 0.337 in. A 3/8 in. leg (throat 0.7 × 0.375 = 0.263 in.) passes; a 5/16 in. leg (throat 0.219 in.) does not.

Now change the neck to NPS 8 Schedule 80, 0.500 in. thick. The thinner part is now 0.500 in., 0.7 × 0.500 = 0.350 in., and the 0.25 in. cap governs, so the required throat is 0.25 in. and the leg 0.357 in. Forget the cap and you get 0.350 ÷ 0.7 = 0.500 in. of leg, which looks conservative but is not what the rule asks for. The Body of Knowledge orients calculation questions towards existing vessels, so expect a weld size question to arrive as part of a repair or alteration rather than new construction.

Welding procedure questions with refinery alloys in mind

The API 510 procedure review is narrower than the welding a Wood River turnaround involves. The Body of Knowledge restricts the WPS, PQR and welder qualification questions to SMAW, GTAW, GMAW and SAW, one process and one filler metal per document, and base metals of P-No. 1, 3, 4, 5 and 8. For the exam it fixes the lower transformation temperature of P-No. 1, 3, 4 and 5 at 1330°F and the upper at 1600°F. That grouping maps neatly onto a hydroprocessing refinery: carbon steel shells, the chromium-molybdenum steels of reactors and hot hydrogen service, and austenitic stainless steel internals and piping.

Overlay, hard-facing and buttered dissimilar metal welds are excluded, even though hydroprocessing reactors often carry stainless overlay, so spend the time on variables, PQR tests and welder qualification range.

Routes to API 510 eligibility from St. Louis jobs

API counts education plus experience gained in the last ten years while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency, and API verifies what you declare. The routes local candidates usually take:

  • NDT technicians who take thickness readings and run MT and PT on Metro East turnarounds. Their work counts when it is inspection activity as the code describes it; the NDT training page for St. Louis covers the ASNT SNT-TC-1A route into that work.
  • Process operators, including graduates of Lewis and Clark Community College's Process Operations Technology programme in Godfrey, whose petroleum degree the college says was developed with Phillips 66 at Wood River. Operating experience helps on the longer routes, but a year of inspection is still required, and API decides whether a two-year qualification counts as engineering or technology.
  • Engineers from programmes such as SIUE's ABET-accredited mechanical engineering degree in Edwardsville or Missouri S&T's metallurgical engineering degree. A bachelor's degree route needs one year of supervising or performing inspection.
  • Welders and fabricators, whose repair and fabrication time counts on the longer routes. Many also prepare for AWS CWI; see AWS CWI exam prep in St. Louis.

The detail of each route is on the API 510 certification page.

Studying for API 510 around a Wood River turnaround

A turnaround can swallow weeks of evenings, so the course is built to pause and restart. A pattern that works: read API 510 and the RP 571 mechanisms while the plant is running steadily; work the Section VIII calculations, UW-16 and UG-99 in particular, in short daily blocks; save questions from the turnaround itself, such as a repair you watched being planned, and put them to the instructor afterwards. Finish with full timed papers.

The examination runs as 2.75 hours closed-book and 3.75 hours open-book with a 45-minute break, and only 140 of the 170 questions are scored. Prometric lists test centres in and around St. Louis; book a seat promptly once API accepts your application, because the window you want may be popular. Exam windows and deadlines are on the API exam schedule page.

Sponsoring API 510 candidates from a St. Louis-area employer

Owner-user departments in the Metro East and inspection contractors on both sides of the river often put several people through API 510 in the same year. A single enquiry can list everyone, and the fees for the group are quoted on request. API still deals with every candidate separately, from the application to the examination seat. In the US, Atlantis also performs UT, MT, PT and VT inspection, described on the pressure vessel inspection page for St. Louis; it does not perform radiography.

faq.q: Can I attend an API 510 class in person in St. Louis?
faq.a: Not with Atlantis. There is no Atlantis classroom in the St. Louis area, and the API 510 course is studied online at your own pace with an instructor answering your questions; you start when you enrol. Some other providers run seminars on fixed dates, and some employers run their own sessions. However you prepare, API's examination is sat in person at a Prometric centre after API accepts your application.

faq.q: Does a Missouri special inspector commission replace API 510 certification?
faq.a: No, they answer different questions. A Missouri special inspector commission, issued under section 650.245 to inspectors of insurers or of companies with an established inspection service for their own vessels, lets you make the inspections the state act requires. API 510 shows you know the in-service code that most refinery and chemical plant vessel programmes are written to. Many owner-user inspectors hold both, and neither is a substitute for the other.

faq.q: Are LPG bullets on the Missouri side inspected by the state, and are they on the exam?
faq.a: Section 650.230 of Missouri's act excludes pressure vessels used to transport and store compressed gases, including LPG containers that meet NFPA or US DOT standards, so a bullet of that kind may fall outside the state certificate system. An owner-user programme can still cover it, so check the owner's programme as well as the state list; on the exam, the same Section VIII and API 510 rules apply to it as to any other vessel.

faq.q: Is naphthenic acid corrosion on the API 510 exam?
faq.a: For the September 2026, January 2027 and May 2027 windows, yes: naphthenic acid corrosion is one of the fifteen RP 571 mechanisms the API 510 Body of Knowledge lists, alongside sulfidation, high-temperature hydrogen attack and wet H2S damage. That suits candidates from a heavy-crude refinery such as Wood River. The API 570 list for its 2027 windows is different and does not include it, so do not assume the two exams share a mechanism list.

faq.q: I inspect deaerators and air receivers at a Missouri plant. Does that count towards API 510?
faq.a: It can, if it is inspection activity of the kind API 510 describes and you did it while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency, and API 510's definition of an authorized inspection agency includes an owner-user's inspection organisation for its own equipment. Thickness surveys, internal inspections and relief device checks on Section VIII vessels are the sort of work API looks for. Document dates, equipment and duties as you go, because API verifies the experience on your application.

faq.q: I have a mechanical engineering degree from SIUE. How soon can I sit API 510?
faq.a: A bachelor's degree in engineering or technology puts you on the shortest route: one year of experience supervising or performing inspection activities as the code describes, gained within the last ten years. Design or project work alone does not meet it, so most graduates build the year inside an owner-user inspection group or with a contractor. Once API accepts the application you choose a window and book a Prometric seat.

faq.q: Can a Metro East contractor enrol a group of API 510 candidates?
faq.a: Yes. Send one enquiry giving the number of candidates, the exam windows they are aiming for and whether any are also preparing for API 570 or API 653, and the quote covers the group. Everyone works through the material separately and puts questions to the instructor, and API handles each application on its own. Staggering candidates across windows keeps a turnaround crew from losing several inspectors to exam week at once.
